prompts.concept: Neighbor-Joining starts from the distance matrix. Which two taxa join first? Pick a cell in the matrix, or click two leaves in a tree.
prompts.math: NJ joins the pair minimizing Q(i,j) = (n−2)·d(i,j) − R_i − R_j. Use the Distance/Q switch to see Q directly — the smallest off-diagonal value wins.

prompts.concept: Four clusters remain. Which pair joins at step 3?
prompts.math: Q is recomputed over the remaining clusters after every join; again the minimum joins.

prompts.concept: Neighbor-Joining recovered the true tree exactly — RF = 0. It assumed nothing about a molecular clock; only that distances are close to additive.
prompts.math: RF counts splits present in one tree but not the other. Two unrooted 6-taxon trees can differ on at most 2·(6−3) = 6 splits.
